sentences.zh: 鎮國勤敏公阿拜，太祖第三子。

translations.literal: Duke Zhenguo Qinmin Gong Abai was the Taizu Emperor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Abai, posthumously Duke Zhenguo Qinmin, was the third son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 天命十年，偕塔拜、巴布泰伐東海北路呼爾哈部，俘千五百戶，還，太祖出城迎勞，授牛錄章京。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianming, together with Tabai and Babutai he campaigned against the Hurha of the northern Eastern Sea route, captured fifteen hundred households; on his return the Taizu Emperor went out of the city to welcome and reward him and appointed him niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 10 he joined Tabai and Babutai in attacking the Hurha of the northern Eastern Sea route, taking fifteen hundred households captive. When he returned, the Taizu Emperor came out of the city to welcome and honor him and made him niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，授梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he was appointed meile ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 he was appointed meile ejen.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，授吏部承政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he was appointed Minister of Personnel, libu chengzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年，封三等鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as third-rank Prince Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as third-rank Prince Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 六年，駐防錦州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was stationed on garrison duty at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was posted to garrison Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，以老，罷承政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, on account of age, he was removed from the post of chengzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, owing to old age, he was dismissed as chengzheng.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，進二等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi he was advanced to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4 his rank was raised to the second degree.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 十年，追封謚。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 阿拜子有爵者三：鞏安，襲三等鎮國將軍，進輔國公；

translations.literal: Of Abai's sons, three held noble rank: Gong'an, who inherited the third-rank Prince Zhenguo and was advanced to Duke Fuguo;
translations.idiomatic: Abai had three sons who held noble rank: Gong'an, who inherited the third-rank Prince Zhenguo and was promoted to Duke Fuguo;

sentences.zh: 乾圖、灝善封輔國公，乾圖謚介直。

translations.literal: Qiantu and Haoshan were enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo; Qiantu received the posthumous title Jiezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantu and Haoshan were enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo; Qiantu was posthumously titled Jiezhi.

sentences.zh: 鞏安、灝善之後，皆以奉恩將軍世襲。

translations.literal: The lines of Gong'an and Haoshan thereafter inherited by feng'en jiangjun in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of Gong'an and Haoshan thereafter held the rank of feng'en jiangjun in perpetual succession.

sentences.zh: 鎮國克潔將軍湯古代，太祖第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Zhenguo Kejie Jiangjun Tanggūdai was the Taizu Emperor's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Tanggūdai, posthumously Prince Zhenguo Kejie, was the fourth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 事太宗，授固山額真。

translations.literal: He served Hong Taiji and was appointed gushan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He served Hong Taiji and was appointed gushan ejen.

sentences.zh: 取永平四城，湯古代偕圖爾格、納穆泰守灤州。

translations.literal: When the four cities of Yongping were taken, Tanggūdai together with Turgūdai and Namutai garrisoned Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the four Yongping cities were captured, Tanggūdai garrisoned Luanzhou together with Turgūdai and Namutai.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，明兵攻灤州急，貝勒阿敏怯不敢援，遣巴都禮率數百人突圍進，夜三鼓，入灤州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong the Ming army pressed the attack on Luanzhou fiercely; Prince Amin, cowed, dared not relieve it and sent Baduli with several hundred men to break through the encirclement and enter; at the third watch of the night they entered Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4 the Ming forces fiercely besieged Luanzhou. Prince Amin, afraid, did not dare to relieve the city and sent Baduli with several hundred men to break through the encirclement; at the third watch of the night they entered Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 既，明兵以炮壞城，城樓火，湯古代等棄城奔永平。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Ming army destroyed the wall with cannon; the gate tower caught fire, and Tanggūdai and the others abandoned the city and fled to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Ming used cannon to breach the wall; the gate tower caught fire, and Tanggūdai and the others abandoned the city and fled to Yongping.

sentences.zh: 既還，太宗廷詰之，湯古代引罪請死。

translations.literal: After they returned, Hong Taiji questioned them at court; Tanggūdai confessed guilt and asked for death.
translations.idiomatic: On their return Hong Taiji questioned them at court; Tanggūdai confessed his fault and asked to die.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「汝不能全師而歸，殺汝何益？

translations.literal: Hong Taiji said: "You could not bring the army back intact—what good would it do to kill you?
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji said, "You failed to bring the army back intact—what good would killing you do?

sentences.zh: 」下所司論罪，免死，罷固山額真，奪所屬人口，籍其家。

translations.literal: " He handed them over to the authorities for judgment; death was remitted, he was removed as gushan ejen, his subordinate population was confiscated, and his household was registered for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He referred the matter to the judicial offices. Tanggūdai was spared death but stripped of his post as gushan ejen, deprived of his subordinate population, and his household was penalized.

sentences.zh: 八年，授三等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed third-rank meile janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed third-rank meile janggin.

sentences.zh: 崇德四年，封三等鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongde he was enfeoffed as third-rank Prince Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 4 he was enfeoffed as third-rank Prince Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 子二：穆爾察，初封三等奉國將軍，襲爵，進二等。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Murca, who was first enfeoffed third-rank fengguo jiangjun, inherited the title, and was advanced to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Murca, first enfeoffed as third-rank fengguo jiangjun, who inherited the title and was promoted to second rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚恪恭；

translations.literal: He died and received the posthumous title Kegong;
translations.idiomatic: on his death he received the posthumous title Kegong;

sentences.zh: 聶克塞，襲穆爾察三等奉國將軍。

translations.literal: Niekesai inherited Murca's third-rank fengguo jiangjun.
translations.idiomatic: Niekesai inherited Murca's third-rank fengguo jiangjun.

sentences.zh: 從多鐸略寧遠，從多爾袞定京師，逐李自成至慶都，皆有功，累進鎮國公。

translations.literal: He followed Dodo in operations against Ningyuan, followed Dorgon in securing the capital, and pursued Li Zicheng to Qingdu, all with merit, and was repeatedly advanced to Duke Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Dodo against Ningyuan, followed Dorgon in securing the capital, and pursued Li Zicheng to Qingdu, earning merit each time until he was repeatedly advanced to Duke Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 坐事降三等鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: For an offense his rank was reduced to third-rank Prince Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was reduced to third-rank Prince Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 4.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son, and the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰，太祖第五子。

translations.literal: Manggūltai was the Taizu Emperor's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai was the fifth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 歲壬子，從太祖伐烏喇，克六城，莽古爾泰請渡水擊之，太祖曰：「止！

translations.literal: In the year renzi he followed the Taizu Emperor in attacking Ula, captured six cities, and Manggūltai asked to cross the water and strike; the Taizu Emperor said: "Stop!
translations.idiomatic: In the renzi year he followed the Taizu Emperor against Ula and took six cities. Manggūltai asked to cross the river and attack. The Taizu Emperor said, "Stop!

sentences.zh: 無僕何以為主？

translations.literal: Without servants, how can one be master?
translations.idiomatic: Without servants, how can one be master?

sentences.zh: 無民何以為君？

translations.literal: Without people, how can one be ruler?
translations.idiomatic: Without people, how can one be ruler?

sentences.zh: 我且削之。

translations.literal: I shall reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: I shall reduce them.

sentences.zh: 」遂毀六城，移軍富勒哈河。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the six cities were destroyed and the army moved to the Fuleha River.
translations.idiomatic: With that the six cities were razed and the army moved to the Fuleha River.

sentences.zh: 越日，於烏喇河建木城，留兵千守焉。

translations.literal: The next day a wooden stockade was built on the Ula River and a thousand men were left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a wooden stockade was built on the Ula River and a thousand men were left to hold it.

sentences.zh: 天命元年，授和碩貝勒，以序稱三貝勒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianming he was appointed Prince of the First Rank, heshuo beile, and, by seniority, was called the Third Beile.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 1 he was appointed heshuo beile and, by order of birth, was called the Third Beile.

sentences.zh: 四年，明經略楊鎬遣總兵杜松以六萬人出撫順關，劉綎以四萬人出寬甸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Grand Secretary Yang Hao of the Ming dispatched Commander Du Song with sixty thousand men out of the Fushun Pass and Liu Ting with forty thousand out of Kuandian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Ming grand secretary Yang Hao sent the commander Du Song with sixty thousand men through the Fushun Pass and Liu Ting with forty thousand through Kuandian.

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰從太祖御松界凡，伏兵薩爾滸谷口，伺明兵過將半擊之，我軍據吉林崖，明兵營薩爾滸山，復偕貝勒代善等以千人益吉林崖，而合師攻薩爾滸，大破之，松戰死。

translations.literal: Manggūltai followed the Taizu Emperor to hold Songjiayan; troops were concealed at the mouth of Sarhū Valley to wait until more than half the Ming army had passed and then strike. Our army held Jilin Cliff while the Ming encamped on Sarhū Mountain; he again joined Princes Daishan and others with a thousand men to reinforce Jilin Cliff, then united forces to attack Sarhū and won a great victory; Song died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai followed the Taizu Emperor to Songjiayan, with troops hidden at the mouth of Sarhū Valley to strike once more than half the Ming force had passed. Our army held Jilin Cliff while the Ming camped on Sarhū Mountain. He again joined Prince Daishan and others with a thousand men to reinforce Jilin Cliff, then united the armies to attack Sarhū, winning a great victory in which Song was killed.

sentences.zh: 又從太祖還軍擊斬綎。

translations.literal: He again followed the Taizu Emperor in turning the army to attack and behead Liu Ting.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the Taizu Emperor as the army turned back to attack and kill Liu Ting.

sentences.zh: 八月，從伐葉赫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he followed in the campaign against Yehe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he joined the campaign against Yehe.

sentences.zh: 五年，太祖伐明，略懿路、蒲城，令莽古爾泰以所部逐敵，率健銳百人追擊明兵，至渾河乃還。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Taizu Emperor campaigned against the Ming, took Yilu and Pucheng, ordered Manggūltai with his command to pursue the enemy, and with a hundred picked troops chased the Ming army to the Hun River before returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Taizu Emperor attacked the Ming, took Yilu and Pucheng, and ordered Manggūltai with his division to pursue the enemy; leading a hundred picked troops he chased the Ming force to the Hun River before returning.

sentences.zh: 六年，鎮江守將陳良策叛投毛文龍，莽古爾泰偕代善遷金州民復州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Zhenjiang garrison commander Chen Liangce rebelled and went over to Mao Wenlong; Manggūltai together with Daishan moved the people of Jinzhou to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Zhenjiang garrison commander Chen Liangce rebelled and defected to Mao Wenlong; Manggūltai and Daishan moved the people of Jinzhou to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，攻剋旅順口。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Lüshunkou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Lüshunkou was captured.

sentences.zh: 察哈爾林丹汗侵科爾沁部，圍克勒珠爾根城，莽古爾泰赴援，至農安塔，林丹汗遁。

translations.literal: Lindan Khan of the Chahar invaded the Khorchin and besieged Kelezhu'ergen; Manggūltai went to relieve them, reached Nong'an Tower, and Lindan Khan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lindan Khan of the Chahar invaded the Khorchin and besieged Kelezhu'ergen. Manggūltai marched to relieve them; when he reached Nong'an Tower, Lindan Khan fled.

sentences.zh: 十一年，太祖伐喀爾喀巴林部，先命諸貝勒略錫拉穆楞，皆以馬乏不能進；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Taizu Emperor campaigned against the Bari of the Khalkha; he first ordered the princes to take Xilamuleng, but all said their horses were exhausted and they could not advance;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Taizu Emperor campaigned against the Bari of the Khalkha and first ordered the princes to take Xilamuleng, but all said their horses were spent and they could not advance;

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰獨領兵夜渡擊之，俘獲無算。

translations.literal: Manggūltai alone led troops across by night and attacked, capturing booty beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai alone led his troops across at night and attacked, taking captives and booty beyond count.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，攻明右屯衛，又以偏師衛塔山糧運。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he attacked the Ming Youdun garrison and also used a detached force to escort grain transport to Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 he attacked the Ming garrison at Youdun and also led a detached force to escort grain transport to Tashan.

sentences.zh: 三年，從太宗徵明，阿巴泰自龍井關入，攻漢兒莊。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Hong Taiji in campaigning against the Ming; Abatai entered through Longjing Pass and attacked Han'erzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Hong Taiji against the Ming; Abatai entered through Longjing Pass and attacked Han'erzhuang.

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰偕多爾袞、多鐸為繼，降其城，旋諭降潘家口守將。

translations.literal: Manggūltai together with Dorgon and Dodo served as reserve; they reduced the city, then were ordered to induce the Panjiakou garrison to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai joined Dorgon and Dodo in the reserve force, took the city, and was then ordered to induce the Panjiakou garrison to surrender.

sentences.zh: 上克洪山口，逼遵化。

translations.literal: The sovereign took Hongshan Pass and pressed Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Hongshan Pass and pressed Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰自漢兒莊合軍擊敗明總兵趙率教，擒其副將臧調元。

translations.literal: Manggūltai united his army with the main force from Han'erzhuang, defeated the Ming commander Zhao Shuaijiao, and captured his deputy Zang Diaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai united with the army from Han'erzhuang, defeated the Ming commander Zhao Shuaijiao, and captured his deputy Zang Diaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 師進次通州，薄明都，明諸道兵入援。

translations.literal: The army advanced and halted at Tongzhou, pressing the Ming capital; Ming troops from every route came to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced to Tongzhou and pressed the Ming capital; Ming forces from every route came to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰遣巴牙喇兵前行，與多鐸殿，值明潰卒來犯，擊殲之。

translations.literal: Manggūltai sent bayara troops ahead and formed the rear with Dodo; they met fleeing Ming troops coming to attack and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai sent bayara troops ahead and formed the rear with Dodo; when broken Ming troops came to attack, they were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 從上閱薊州，破山海關援兵。

translations.literal: He followed the sovereign in reviewing Jizhou and broke the Shanhaiguan relief army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor in reconnoitering Jizhou and defeated the Shanhaiguan relief force.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，克永平、遵化。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Yongping and Zunhua were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Yongping and Zunhua were captured.

sentences.zh: 還，與明兵遇，敗之。

translations.literal: On the return they met Ming troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the march back they met Ming troops and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 五年，從圍大凌河，正藍旗圍其南，莽古爾泰與德格類率巴牙喇兵策應。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed in the siege of Dalinghe; the Plain Blue Banner invested the south, and Manggūltai with Degesi led bayara troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined the siege of Dalinghe; the Plain Blue Banner invested the south, while Manggūltai and Degesi led bayara troops in support.

sentences.zh: 明總兵吳襄、監軍道張春赴援，距城十五里而營。

translations.literal: The Ming commander Wu Xiang and the supervising secretary Zhang Chun came to relieve the city and encamped fifteen li away.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming commander Wu Xiang and the supervising secretary Zhang Chun came to relieve the city and encamped fifteen li away.

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰從上擊之，獲春等。

translations.literal: Manggūltai followed the sovereign in attacking them and captured Chun and others.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai followed the emperor in attacking them and captured Chun and others.

sentences.zh: 當圍大凌河時，莽古爾泰以所部兵被創，言於上。

translations.literal: During the siege of Dalinghe, Manggūltai's troops had suffered wounds, and he spoke of it to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: While Dalinghe was under siege, Manggūltai's troops had been wounded, and he reported this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上偶詰之曰：「聞爾所部兵每有違誤。

translations.literal: The sovereign happened to question him, saying: "I hear that your troops are often at fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor happened to question him, saying, "I hear your troops are often at fault.

sentences.zh: 」莽古爾泰恚曰：「寧有是耶？

translations.literal: Manggūltai angrily said: "Could that really be so?
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai said in anger, "Could that really be so?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「若告者誣，當治告者；

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "If the informant is lying, the informant should be punished;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If the informant is lying, the informant should be punished;

sentences.zh: 果實，爾所部兵豈得無罪？

translations.literal: if it is true, can your troops be without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: if it is true, can your troops be without guilt?

sentences.zh: 」言已，將起乘馬，莽古爾泰曰：「上何獨與我為難？

translations.literal: " When he had spoken he was about to mount his horse; Manggūltai said: "Why does Your Majesty single me out for difficulty?
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished speaking he was about to mount his horse. Manggūltai said, "Why does Your Majesty single me out?

sentences.zh: 我固承順，乃猶欲殺我耶？

translations.literal: I have always submitted—yet You still wish to kill me?
translations.idiomatic: I have always submitted—yet You still wish to kill me?

sentences.zh: 」撫佩刀，頻目之。

translations.literal: He stroked the sword at his belt and glared repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: He stroked the sword at his belt and glared repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 貝勒德格類，其母弟也，斥其悖，拳毆之，莽古爾泰益怒，抽刃出鞘。

translations.literal: Prince Degesi, his younger brother by the same mother, rebuked his insubordination and struck him with his fist; Manggūltai grew angrier and drew his blade from the scabbard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Degesi, his younger brother by the same mother, rebuked his insubordination and struck him with his fist; Manggūltai grew still angrier and drew his blade from the scabbard.

sentences.zh: 左右揮之出，上憤曰：「是固嘗弒其母以邀寵者！

translations.literal: Attendants hustled him out; the sovereign said in anger: "He is the one who once killed his mother to win favor!
translations.idiomatic: Attendants hustled him out. The emperor said angrily, "He is the one who once killed his mother to win favor!

sentences.zh: 」諸貝勒議莽古爾泰大不敬，奪和碩貝勒，降多羅貝勒，削五牛錄，罰銀萬及甲胄、雕鞍馬十、素鞍馬二。

translations.literal: The princes judged that Manggūltai had committed grave disrespect; he was deprived of the rank of heshuo beile, reduced to doroi beile, stripped of five niru, and fined ten thousand taels of silver plus armor, ten carved-saddle horses, and two plain-saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: The princes judged Manggūltai guilty of grave disrespect; he was deprived of heshuo beile, reduced to doroi beile, stripped of five niru, and fined ten thousand taels of silver plus armor, ten carved-saddle horses, and two plain-saddle horses.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐察哈爾，林丹汗遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the campaign against the Chahar; Lindan Khan fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the campaign against the Chahar; Lindan Khan fled.

sentences.zh: 移師伐明，略大同、宣府。

translations.literal: The army shifted to attack the Ming and took Datong and Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: The army shifted to attack the Ming and took Datong and Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，卒，上臨喪，漏盡三鼓，始還；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died; the sovereign attended the mourning and did not return until the third watch had run out;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died. The emperor attended the mourning and did not return until the third watch had run out;

sentences.zh: 又於中門設幄以祭，哭之慟，乃入宮。

translations.literal: he also set up a mourning tent at the middle gate and wept bitterly before entering the palace.
translations.idiomatic: he also set up a mourning tent at the middle gate and wept bitterly before entering the palace.

sentences.zh: 九年，莽古爾泰女弟莽古濟格格所屬冷僧機告莽古爾泰與德格類、莽古濟格格盟誓怨望，將危上，以莽古濟格格夫瑣諾木為證。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Manggūltai's younger sister, Princess Manggūji, had a subordinate named Lengsengji report that Manggūltai, Degesi, and Princess Manggūji had sworn an oath in resentment and intended to endanger the sovereign, with Manggūji's husband Suonuomu as witness.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Manggūltai's younger sister Princess Manggūji had a subordinate named Lengsengji report that Manggūltai, Degesi, and Princess Manggūji had sworn an oath in resentment and intended to harm the emperor, with Manggūji's husband Suonuomu as witness.

sentences.zh: 搜得牌印十六，文曰「大金國皇帝之印」。

translations.literal: Sixteen seals were found bearing the inscription "Seal of the Emperor of the Great Jin State."
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen seals were found bearing the inscription "Seal of the Emperor of the Great Jin State."

sentences.zh: 追奪莽古爾泰爵。

translations.literal: Manggūltai's title was posthumously revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai's title was posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 莽古濟格格及莽古爾泰子額必倫坐死，餘子並黜宗室。

translations.literal: Princess Manggūji and Manggūltai's son Ebilun were sentenced to death; the remaining sons were all expelled from the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Manggūji and Manggūltai's son Ebilun were sentenced to death; the remaining sons were all expelled from the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 輔國愨厚公塔拜，太祖第六子。

translations.literal: Duke Fuguo Kehou Gong Tabai was the Taizu Emperor's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Tabai, posthumously Duke Fuguo Kehou, was the sixth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 天命十年，伐東海北路呼爾哈部有功，授三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianming he campaigned against the Hurha of the northern Eastern Sea route with merit and was appointed third-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 10 he campaigned against the Hurha of the northern Eastern Sea route with merit and was appointed third-rank jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，進一等。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he was advanced to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 he was advanced to first rank.

sentences.zh: 尋封三等輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed third-rank Duke Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enfeoffed as third-rank Duke Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 崇德四年九月，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Chongde he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Chongde 4.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，追封謚。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 塔拜子八，有爵者三：額克親、班布爾善、巴都海。

translations.literal: Tabai had eight sons; three held noble rank: Ekeqin, Banbuerhan, and Baduhai.
translations.idiomatic: Tabai had eight sons; three held noble rank: Ekeqin, Banbuerhan, and Baduhai.

sentences.zh: 額克親，崇德元年，從阿濟格伐明，偪燕京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde Ekeqin followed Ajige in campaigning against the Ming and pressed Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 Ekeqin followed Ajige against the Ming and pressed Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 明兵自涿州來拒，親陷陣，破之。

translations.literal: Ming troops came from Zhuozhou to resist; he charged into the formation in person and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Ming troops came from Zhuozhou to resist; he charged into the formation himself and broke them.

sentences.zh: 四年，封三等奉國將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed third-rank fengguo jiangjun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as third-rank fengguo jiangjun.

sentences.zh: 尋襲爵。

translations.literal: Soon he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 五年，從多爾袞攻錦州，復從多鐸追擊明兵於塔山。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Dorgon in attacking Jinzhou and again followed Dodo in pursuing Ming troops at Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Dorgon in attacking Jinzhou and again followed Dodo in pursuing Ming troops at Tashan.

sentences.zh: 六年，上圍錦州，敗洪承疇兵十三萬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the sovereign besieged Jinzhou and defeated Hong Chengchou's army of one hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor besieged Jinzhou and defeated Hong Chengchou's army of one hundred thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 移軍近松山，掘壕困之。

translations.literal: The army moved near Songshan and dug trenches to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: The army moved near Songshan and dug trenches to hem them in.

sentences.zh: 明總兵曹變蛟夜突上營，額克親偕內大臣錫翰力御，卻之。

translations.literal: The Ming commander Cao Bianjiao made a night sortie against the imperial camp; Ekeqin together with the inner minister Xihen resisted fiercely and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming commander Cao Bianjiao made a night sortie against the imperial camp; Ekeqin together with the inner minister Xihen resisted fiercely and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 敘功，賜銀八十。

translations.literal: For merit he was rewarded with eighty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was rewarded with eighty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從多爾袞入山海關，破李自成，有功，累進鎮國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed Dorgon through Shanhaiguan, defeated Li Zicheng with merit, and was repeatedly advanced to Duke Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he followed Dorgon through Shanhaiguan, defeated Li Zicheng with merit, and was repeatedly advanced to Duke Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 七年，授正白旗滿洲固山額真，復進貝子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed gushan ejen of the Plain White Banner Manchu and was again advanced to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed gushan ejen of the Plain White Banner Manchu and was again advanced to beizi.

sentences.zh: 八年，坐附羅什博爾惠諂媚諸王造言構釁，削爵，黜宗室。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, on account of siding with Rosi and Bolhui in flattering the princes and fabricating words to stir up quarrels, his title was stripped and he was expelled from the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was convicted for siding with Rosi and Bolhui in flattering the princes and fabricating slander to stir up strife; his title was stripped and he was expelled from the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 九年，復入宗室，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was readmitted to the imperial clan and appointed inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was readmitted to the imperial clan and appointed inner minister.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died.

sentences.zh: 班布爾善，累進封輔國公。

translations.literal: Banbuerhan was repeatedly advanced and enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Banbuerhan was repeatedly advanced until he was enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 以附鰲拜，譴死。

translations.literal: For siding with Oboi he was condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: For siding with Oboi he was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 附見鰲拜傳。

translations.literal: See the attached account in the biography of Oboi.
translations.idiomatic: See the biography of Oboi.

sentences.zh: 巴都海，亦封輔國公，謚恪僖。

translations.literal: Baduhai was also enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo, with posthumous title Keyi.
translations.idiomatic: Baduhai was also enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo, with the posthumous title Keyi.

sentences.zh: 饒餘敏郡王阿巴泰，太祖第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Rao Yu Min junwang Abatai was the Taizu Emperor's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Abatai, posthumously Prince Rao Yu Min, was the seventh son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 初授台吉。

translations.literal: He was first granted the title taiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was first granted the title taiji.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥，與費英東、安費揚古率師伐東海窩集部烏爾固辰、穆棱二路，俘千餘人，還。

translations.literal: In the xinhai year, together with Fiongondo and Eyanggu he led troops against the Woji of the Eastern Sea, the Wuergerchen and Muling routes, captured more than a thousand people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinhai year he joined Fiongondo and Eyanggu in campaigning against the Woji of the Eastern Sea along the Wuergerchen and Muling routes, taking more than a thousand captives before returning.

sentences.zh: 天命八年，偕台吉德格類等伐紥嚕特部，渡遼河，擊部長昂安。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianming, together with taiji Degesi and others he campaigned against the Jalut; crossing the Liao River they attacked the chief Angan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 8, together with taiji Degesi and others, he campaigned against the Jalut; crossing the Liao River they attacked the chief Angan.

sentences.zh: 昂安攜妻子引牛車遁，師從之，昂邦章京達音布戰死。

translations.literal: Angan fled with his wife and children in ox carts; the army pursued. Angbang janggin Dayinbu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Angan fled with his wife and children in ox carts; the army pursued. Angbang janggin Dayinbu was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 阿巴泰繼進，斬昂安及其子，俘其眾，還，太祖郊勞，並賚從徵將士。

translations.literal: Abatai pressed forward, beheaded Angan and his son, captured his followers, and returned. The Taizu Emperor welcomed him beyond the suburbs and rewarded the officers who had joined the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Abatai pressed on, beheaded Angan and his son, and took his followers captive. On his return the Taizu Emperor welcomed him beyond the suburbs and rewarded the officers who had joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，封貝勒。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded, Abatai was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji acceded, Abatai was enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 阿巴泰語額駙揚古利、達爾漢曰：「戰則擐甲胄，獵則佩弓矢，何不得為和碩貝勒？

translations.literal: Abatai said to efang Yangguli and Darhan: "In battle one dons armor; in the hunt one carries bow and arrows—why should one not be heshuo beile?
translations.idiomatic: Abatai said to efang Yangguli and Darhan, "In battle one dons armor; in the hunt one carries bow and arrows—why should one not be heshuo beile?

sentences.zh: 」語聞，上曰：「爾等宜勸之，告朕何為？

translations.literal: When the words were reported, the emperor said: "You ought to persuade him—why tell me?
translations.idiomatic: When the words were reported, the emperor said, "You ought to persuade him—why tell me?

sentences.zh: 」天聰元年，察哈爾昂坤杜棱來歸，與宴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong, Angkun Duleng of the Chahar came to submit and joined the feast.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 Angkun Duleng of the Chahar came to submit and was invited to the feast.

sentences.zh: 阿巴泰不出，曰：「我與諸小貝勒同列。

translations.literal: Abatai did not attend, saying: "I rank with the junior beile.
translations.idiomatic: Abatai did not attend, saying, "I rank with the junior beile.

sentences.zh: 蒙古貝勒明安巴克乃位我上，我恥之！

translations.literal: The Mongol beile Ming'an Baknai was seated above me—I am ashamed of it!
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol beile Ming'an Baknai was seated above me—I am ashamed of it!

sentences.zh: 」上以語諸貝勒，貝勒代善與諸貝勒共責之曰：「德格類、濟爾哈朗、杜度、岳託、碩託早從五大臣議政，爾不預焉。

translations.literal: The emperor told the beile; Prince Daishan together with the beile jointly rebuked him, saying: "Degesi, Jirhalang, Dudu, Yueto, and Shuoto took part early in the Five Ministers' deliberations—you were not among them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the beile. Prince Daishan together with the beile jointly rebuked him, saying, "Degesi, Jirhalang, Dudu, Yueto, and Shuoto took part early in the Five Ministers' deliberations—you were not among them.

sentences.zh: 阿濟格、多爾袞，多鐸，先帝時使領全旗，諸貝勒皆先爾入八分。

translations.literal: Ajige, Dorgon, and Dodo were made to command whole banners in the Late Emperor's time; all the beile entered the Eight Shares before you.
translations.idiomatic: Ajige, Dorgon, and Dodo were made to command whole banners in the Late Emperor's time; all the beile entered the Eight Shares before you.

sentences.zh: 爾今為貝勒，得六牛錄，已逾分矣！

translations.literal: You are now a beile with six niru—that already exceeds your due!
translations.idiomatic: You are now a beile with six niru—that already exceeds your due!

sentences.zh: 乃欲與和碩貝勒抗行，得和碩貝勒，不更將覬覦耶？

translations.literal: Yet you wish to stand equal with heshuo beile; if you became heshuo beile, would you not covet still more?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you wish to stand equal with heshuo beile; if you became heshuo beile, would you not covet still more?

sentences.zh: 」阿巴泰引罪，罰甲胄、雕鞍馬四、素鞍馬八。

translations.literal: Abatai acknowledged guilt; he was fined armor, four carved-saddle horses, and eight plain-saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: Abatai acknowledged guilt and was fined armor, four carved-saddle horses, and eight plain-saddle horses.

sentences.zh: 二年，與岳託、碩託伐錦州，明師退守寧遠，克墩台二十一，毀錦州、杏山、高橋三城，還。

translations.literal: In the second year, together with Yueto and Shuoto he attacked Jinzhou. The Ming army withdrew to defend Ningyuan; twenty-one blockhouses were taken and the three cities of Jinzhou, Xingshan, and Gaoqiao were destroyed before they returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he joined Yueto and Shuoto in attacking Jinzhou. The Ming army withdrew to defend Ningyuan; twenty-one blockhouses were taken and the three cities of Jinzhou, Xingshan, and Gaoqiao were destroyed before they returned.

sentences.zh: 三年，從伐明，自喀喇沁波羅河屯行七日，偕阿濟格率左翼四旗及蒙古軍攻龍井關，夜半克之。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the campaign against the Ming. From Khalkha Boluohetun they marched seven days; together with Ajige he led the Left Wing's four banners and Mongol troops to attack Longjing Pass and took it at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed the campaign against the Ming. From Khalkha Boluohetun they marched seven days; together with Ajige he led the Left Wing's four banners and Mongol troops to attack Longjing Pass and took it at midnight.

sentences.zh: 明將易愛自漢兒莊赴援，擊斬之，取其城。

translations.literal: The Ming commander Yi Ai came from Han'erzhuang to relieve; he was struck down and killed, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming commander Yi Ai came from Han'erzhuang to relieve the city; he was struck down and killed, and the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 會上克洪山口，逼遵化，敗明山海關援兵，克之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the emperor took Hongshan Pass and pressed Zunhua, defeated Ming relief from Shanhaiguan, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the emperor took Hongshan Pass and pressed Zunhua, defeated Ming relief from Shanhaiguan, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 復趨通州，明總兵滿桂、侯世祿屯順義，阿巴泰偕岳託擊走之，獲馬千餘、駝百，順義亦下。

translations.literal: They then pressed Tongzhou. Ming commander-in-chief Man Gui and Hou Shilu were encamped at Shunyi; Abatai together with Yueto drove them off, taking more than a thousand horses and a hundred camels; Shunyi also fell.
translations.idiomatic: They then pressed Tongzhou. Ming commander-in-chief Man Gui and Hou Shilu were encamped at Shunyi; Abatai together with Yueto drove them off, taking more than a thousand horses and a hundred camels, and Shunyi also fell.

sentences.zh: 時袁崇煥、祖大壽以兵二萬屯廣渠門外，阿巴泰偕莽古爾泰等率師攻之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou had twenty thousand troops encamped outside Guangqi Gate; Abatai together with Manggūltai and others led forces to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou had twenty thousand troops encamped outside Guangqi Gate; Abatai together with Manggūltai and others led forces to attack them.

sentences.zh: 聞敵伏兵於右，諸貝勒相約入隘必趨右，若出中路，與避敵同。

translations.literal: Hearing the enemy had ambushed on the right, the beile agreed that entering the pass one must head right; to go by the middle road would be the same as avoiding the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the enemy had ambushed on the right, the beile agreed that entering the pass one must head right; to go by the middle road would be the same as avoiding the enemy.

sentences.zh: 豪格趨右，敗伏兵，轉戰至城壕。

translations.literal: Hooge headed right, defeated the ambush, and fought on to the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Hooge headed right, defeated the ambush, and fought on to the moat.

sentences.zh: 阿巴泰出中路，亦破敵，與豪格師會。

translations.literal: Abatai went by the middle road, also defeated the enemy, and united with Hooge's force.
translations.idiomatic: Abatai went by the middle road, also defeated the enemy, and united with Hooge's force.

sentences.zh: 罷戰，諸貝勒議違約罪，阿巴泰當削爵。

translations.literal: When fighting ceased the beile debated the breach of agreement; Abatai was to be stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting ceased the beile debated the breach of agreement; Abatai was to be stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「阿巴泰非怯，以顧其二子，與豪格相失，朕奈何加罪於吾兄？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Abatai is not cowardly; he was watching out for his two sons and lost contact with Hooge—how can I punish my elder brother?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Abatai is not cowardly; he was watching out for his two sons and lost contact with Hooge—how can I punish my elder brother?

sentences.zh: 」宥之。

translations.literal: " He was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 徇通州，焚其舟，略張家灣。

translations.literal: They raided Tongzhou, burned their boats, and plundered Zhangjiawan.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Tongzhou, burned their boats, and plundered Zhangjiawan.

sentences.zh: 從上至薊州，明兵五千自山海關至，奮擊，殲其眾。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Jizhou; five thousand Ming troops came from Shanhaiguan; our forces fought fiercely and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor to Jizhou; five thousand Ming troops came from Shanhaiguan; our forces fought fiercely and annihilated them.

sentences.zh: 四年，從上圍永平，與濟爾哈朗邀斬叛將劉興祚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the emperor in besieging Yongping and, together with Jirhalang, intercepted and killed the rebel commander Liu Xingzuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed the emperor in besieging Yongping and, together with Jirhalang, intercepted and killed the rebel commander Liu Xingzuo.

sentences.zh: 尋命守永平。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to garrison Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to garrison Yongping.

sentences.zh: 明兵攻灤州，偕薩哈璘赴援，明兵引退，代還。

translations.literal: When Ming troops attacked Luanzhou he went with Sahaliyan to relieve; the Ming withdrew and he returned in Daishan's place.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming troops attacked Luanzhou he went with Sahaliyan to relieve the city; the Ming withdrew and he returned in Daishan's place.

sentences.zh: 五年，初設六部，掌工部事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Six Ministries were first established; he directed the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Six Ministries were first established; he directed the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 從上圍大凌河，正黃旗圍北之西，鑲黃旗圍北之東，阿巴泰率巴牙喇兵為策應。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor in besieging Dalinghe; the Plain Yellow Banner invested the northwest, the Bordered Yellow the northeast, and Abatai led bayara troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor in besieging Dalinghe; the Plain Yellow Banner invested the northwest, the Bordered Yellow the northeast, and Abatai led bayara troops in support.

sentences.zh: 大壽降，阿巴泰偕德格類、多爾袞、岳託以兵四千易漢裝，從大壽夜襲錦州，二更行，炮發不絕聲。

translations.literal: When Dashou surrendered, Abatai together with Degesi, Dorgon, and Yueto with four thousand men in Han dress followed Dashou in a night raid on Jinzhou; at the second watch they set out, cannon firing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Dashou surrendered, Abatai together with Degesi, Dorgon, and Yueto led four thousand men in Han dress with Dashou in a night raid on Jinzhou; at the second watch they set out, cannon firing without cease.

sentences.zh: 錦州人聞之，謂大凌河兵逸，爭出應之，師縱擊，斬馘甚眾。

translations.literal: The people of Jinzhou heard it and thought troops had escaped from Dalinghe; they rushed out in response and our army attacked, killing very many.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jinzhou heard it and thought troops had escaped from Dalinghe; they rushed out in response and our army attacked, killing very many.

sentences.zh: 霧，兩軍皆失伍，乃引還。

translations.literal: Fog came; both armies lost formation, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fog came; both armies lost formation, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七年，築蘭磐城，賜御用蟒衣一、紫貂皮八、馬一。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he built Lanpan Fortress and was given one imperial python robe, eight sables, and one horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he built Lanpan Fortress and was given one imperial python robe, eight sables, and one horse.

sentences.zh: 詔問徵明及北韓、察哈爾三者何先，阿巴泰請先伐明。

translations.literal: An edict asked which should come first—campaign against the Ming, northern Korea, or Chahar; Abatai asked to attack the Ming first.
translations.idiomatic: An edict asked which should come first—campaign against the Ming, northern Korea, or Chahar; Abatai asked to attack the Ming first.

sentences.zh: 八月，略山海關，俘數千人還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he raided Shanhaiguan, captured several thousand people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he raided Shanhaiguan, captured several thousand people, and returned.

sentences.zh: 上迎勞，責其不深入。

translations.literal: The emperor came out to welcome and reproved him for not penetrating deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came out to welcome and reproved him for not penetrating deeply.

sentences.zh: 八年，從徵宣府，至應州，克靈丘及王家莊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed the expedition to Xuanfu, reached Yingzhou, and took Lingqiu and Wangjiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he followed the expedition to Xuanfu, reached Yingzhou, and took Lingqiu and Wangjiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 九年，阿巴泰病手痛，上曰：「爾自謂手痛不耐勞苦。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Abatai fell ill with hand pain; the emperor said: "You claim your hand pains and you cannot endure hardship.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Abatai fell ill with hand pain; the emperor said, "You claim your hand pains and you cannot endure hardship.

sentences.zh: 不知人身血脈，勞則無滯。

translations.literal: You do not know that in the human body blood and channels—when one labors there is no stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: You do not know that in the human body blood and channels—when one labors there is no stagnation.

sentences.zh: 惟家居佚樂，不涉郊原，手不持弓矢，忽爾勞動，疾痛易生。

translations.literal: Only living at home in ease, never going to the open country, never holding bow and arrows—then if you suddenly exert yourself, pain comes easily.
translations.idiomatic: Only living at home in ease, never going to the open country, never holding bow and arrows—then if you suddenly exert yourself, pain comes easily.

sentences.zh: 若日以騎射為事，寧復患此？

translations.literal: If you took riding and archery as your daily business, would you still suffer this?
translations.idiomatic: If you took riding and archery as your daily business, would you still suffer this?

sentences.zh: 凡有統帥之責者，非躬自教練，士卒奚由奮？

translations.literal: All who bear command must train in person—otherwise by what means would the troops be roused?
translations.idiomatic: All who bear command must train in person—otherwise by what means would the troops be roused?

sentences.zh: 爾毋媮安，斯克敵制勝，身不期強而自強矣。

translations.literal: Do not be indolent; then you can overcome the enemy and triumph, and strength comes without seeking it.
translations.idiomatic: Do not be indolent; then you can overcome the enemy and triumph, and strength comes without seeking it.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，封饒餘貝勒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he was enfeoffed as Prince Rao Yu beile.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he was enfeoffed as Prince Rao Yu beile.

sentences.zh: 偕阿濟格等伐明，克雕鶚堡、長安嶺堡，薄延慶，分兵克定興、安肅、容城、安州、雄、東安、文安、寶坻、順義、昌平十城。

translations.literal: Together with Ajige and others he campaigned against the Ming, took Diaoge Fort and Chang'anling Fort, pressed Yanqing, and detached forces to take ten cities: Dingxing, Ansu, Rongcheng, Anzhou, Xiong, Dong'an, Wen'an, Baodi, Shunyi, and Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Ajige and others he campaigned against the Ming, took Diaoge Fort and Chang'anling Fort, pressed Yanqing, and detached forces to take ten cities: Dingxing, Ansu, Rongcheng, Anzhou, Xiong, Dong'an, Wen'an, Baodi, Shunyi, and Changping.

sentences.zh: 五十六戰皆捷，俘十數萬。

translations.literal: Fifty-six battles were all won; captives numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-six battles were all won; captives numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 師還，上出城十里迎勞，酌以金卮。

translations.literal: When the army returned the emperor came out ten li beyond the city to welcome and reward them and poured wine from a golden goblet.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned the emperor came out ten li beyond the city to welcome and reward them and poured wine from a golden goblet.

sentences.zh: 上伐北韓，留防噶海城。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against northern Korea he remained to guard Gahai Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against northern Korea he remained to guard Gahai Fortress.

sentences.zh: 三年，上伐喀爾喀，阿巴泰與代善留守，築遼陽都爾弼城，復治盛京至遼河道，道廣十丈，高三尺，濬壕夾之。

translations.literal: In the third year when the emperor campaigned against the Khalkha, Abatai and Daishan remained on guard; they built the Durbi fortress at Liaoyang and again repaired the road from Mukden to Liaoyang—ten zhang wide, three chi high, with moats dredged on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year when the emperor campaigned against the Khalkha, Abatai and Daishan remained on guard; they built the Durbi fortress at Liaoyang and again repaired the road from Mukden to Liaoyang—ten zhang wide, three chi high, with moats dredged on both sides.

sentences.zh: 副多爾袞率師伐明，毀邊牆入，越明都趨涿州，直抵山西。

translations.literal: Assisting Dorgon he led troops against the Ming, broke through the border wall, passed the Ming capital toward Zhuozhou, and reached straight into Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting Dorgon he led troops against the Ming, broke through the border wall, passed the Ming capital toward Zhuozhou, and pressed straight into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 復東趨臨清，克濟南。

translations.literal: Turning east they pressed Linqing and took Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Turning east they pressed Linqing and took Jinan.

sentences.zh: 略天津、遷安，出青山關，還。

translations.literal: They raided Tianjin and Qian'an and exited through Qingshan Pass before returning.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Tianjin and Qian'an and exited through Qingshan Pass before returning.

sentences.zh: 賜馬二、銀五千。

translations.literal: He was given two horses and five thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He was given two horses and five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 四年，偕阿濟格略錦州、寧遠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, together with Ajige, he raided Jinzhou and Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, together with Ajige, he raided Jinzhou and Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 五年，偕多爾袞屯田義州，分兵克錦州城西九台，刈其禾；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with Dorgon he garrisoned Yizhou for farming; detached forces took nine fortresses west of Jinzhou and reaped the grain;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, together with Dorgon he garrisoned Yizhou for farming; detached forces took nine fortresses west of Jinzhou and reaped the grain;

sentences.zh: 又克小凌河西二台。

translations.literal: They also took two fortresses west of the Xiaoling River.
translations.idiomatic: They also took two fortresses west of the Xiaoling River.

sentences.zh: 偕杜度伏兵寧遠，截明運道，奪米千石。

translations.literal: Together with Dudu he ambushed at Ningyuan, cut the Ming supply route, and seized a thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Dudu he ambushed at Ningyuan, cut the Ming supply route, and seized a thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 移師敗明杏山、松山兵。

translations.literal: Moving the army he defeated Ming forces at Xingshan and Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: Moving the army he defeated Ming forces at Xingshan and Songshan.

sentences.zh: 時大軍更番圍錦州，阿巴泰屢往還其間。

translations.literal: At that time the main army took turns besieging Jinzhou; Abatai went back and forth repeatedly among them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the main army took turns besieging Jinzhou; Abatai went back and forth repeatedly among them.

sentences.zh: 六年，坐從多爾袞去錦州三十里為營及遣士卒還家，論削爵，奪所屬戶口。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on account of following Dorgon in encamping thirty li from Jinzhou and sending troops home, he was sentenced to lose his rank and forfeit his subordinate households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on account of following Dorgon in encamping thirty li from Jinzhou and sending troops home, he was sentenced to lose his rank and forfeit his subordinate households.

sentences.zh: 詔寬之，罰銀二千。

translations.literal: An edict leniently reduced the penalty to a fine of two thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: An edict leniently reduced the penalty to a fine of two thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 尋從上破洪承疇援兵十三萬。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the emperor in defeating Hong Chengchou's relief army of one hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed the emperor in defeating Hong Chengchou's relief army of one hundred thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 七年，錦州降，偕濟爾哈朗圍杏山，克之，還守錦州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Jinzhou surrendered; together with Jirhalang he besieged Xingshan, took it, and returned to garrison Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Jinzhou surrendered; together with Jirhalang he besieged Xingshan, took it, and returned to garrison Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 敘功，賜蟒緞七十。

translations.literal: For merit he was given seventy rolls of python brocade.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was given seventy rolls of python brocade.

sentences.zh: 十月，授奉命大將軍伐明，內大臣圖爾格副之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was appointed Commander-in-Chief by Imperial Order to campaign against the Ming, with Inner Minister Turgūdai as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was appointed Commander-in-Chief by Imperial Order to campaign against the Ming, with Inner Minister Turgūdai as deputy.

sentences.zh: 自黃崖口入邊，敗明將白騰蛟等於薊州，破河間、景州。

translations.literal: Entering the border at Huangyakou he defeated Ming generals Bai Tengjiao and others at Jizhou and broke Hejian and Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the border at Huangyakou he defeated Ming generals Bai Tengjiao and others at Jizhou and broke Hejian and Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 趨兗州，擒斬明魯王以派等。

translations.literal: Pressing Yanzhou he captured and beheaded the Ming Prince of Lu Yipai and others.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing Yanzhou he captured and beheaded the Ming Prince of Lu Yipai and others.

sentences.zh: 分徇萊州、登州、青州、莒州、沂州，南至海州。

translations.literal: Detached columns raided Laizhou, Dengzhou, Qingzhou, Juzhou, and Yizhou, reaching south to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Detached columns raided Laizhou, Dengzhou, Qingzhou, Juzhou, and Yizhou, reaching south to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 還略滄州、天津、三河、密雲。

translations.literal: On the return they raided Cangzhou, Tianjin, Sanhe, and Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: On the return they raided Cangzhou, Tianjin, Sanhe, and Miyun.

sentences.zh: 凡克城八十八，降城六，俘三十六萬，得金萬二千、銀二百二十萬有奇。

translations.literal: In all they took eighty-eight cities, received the surrender of six, captured three hundred sixty thousand, and obtained more than twelve thousand jin of gold and over two million two hundred thousand of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In all they took eighty-eight cities, received the surrender of six, captured three hundred sixty thousand, and obtained more than twelve thousand jin of gold and over two million two hundred thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，師還，上遣濟爾哈朗、多爾袞等郊迎三十里，賜銀萬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year the army returned; the emperor sent Jirhalang, Dorgon, and others to welcome them thirty li beyond the suburbs and gave ten thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year the army returned; the emperor sent Jirhalang, Dorgon, and others to welcome them thirty li beyond the suburbs and gave ten thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 順治元年四月，進郡王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shunzhi he was advanced to junwang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 1 he was advanced to junwang.

sentences.zh: 二年，統左右兩翼兵鎮山東，剿滿家洞土寇，尋還。

translations.literal: In the second year he commanded the Left and Right Wings in garrisoning Shandong, suppressed the bandits of Manjiadong, and soon returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he commanded the Left and Right Wings in garrisoning Shandong, suppressed the bandits of Manjiadong, and soon returned.

sentences.zh: 三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，追謚。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi posthumous honors were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 posthumous honors were conferred.

sentences.zh: 阿巴泰子五，有爵者四：尚建、博和託、博洛、岳樂，而岳樂襲爵。

translations.literal: Abatai had five sons; four held rank: Shangjian, Bohetuo, Boluo, and Yuele—and Yuele inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Abatai had five sons; four held rank: Shangjian, Bohetuo, Boluo, and Yuele—and Yuele inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 安和親王岳樂，阿巴泰第四子。

translations.literal: Prince An Heqin Yuele was Abatai's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele, posthumously Prince An Heqin, was Abatai's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初封鎮國公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Duke Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，從豪格徇四川，擊斬張獻忠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he followed Hooge in pacifying Sichuan and struck down Zhang Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he followed Hooge in pacifying Sichuan and struck down Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 六年，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 八年，襲爵，改號安郡王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he inherited the title and the designation was changed to Prince An junwang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he inherited the title and the designation was changed to Prince An junwang.

sentences.zh: 九年，掌工部事，與議政。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he directed the Ministry of Works and joined in deliberation of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he directed the Ministry of Works and joined in deliberation of state.

sentences.zh: 十年，命為宣威大將軍，駐歸化城，規討喀爾喀部土謝圖汗、車臣汗。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed General Xuanwei, stationed at Guihuacheng, and planned to subdue the Khalkha Tüsiyetü Khan and Setsen Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed General Xuanwei, stationed at Guihuacheng, and planned to subdue the Khalkha Tüsiyetü Khan and Setsen Khan.

sentences.zh: 尋行成，入貢，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: Soon peace was concluded and tribute was offered, so troops were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Soon peace was concluded and tribute was offered, so troops were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 十二年，掌宗人府事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he directed the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he directed the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進親王。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 he was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，吳三桂、耿精忠並反，犯江西。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong both rebelled and invaded Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13, Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong both rebelled and invaded Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 命為定遠平寇大將軍，率師討之，自江西規廣東，次南昌，遣兵復安福、都昌。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pacification Commissioner General for the Distant Pacification of Bandits, led an army to attack them, planned from Jiangxi toward Guangdong, halted at Nanchang, and sent troops to recover Anfu and Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Pacification Commissioner General for the Distant Pacification of Bandits, led an army against them, aimed from Jiangxi at Guangdong, halted at Nanchang, and sent troops to recover Anfu and Duchang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，覆上高、新昌。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he recovered Shanggao and Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 he recovered Shanggao and Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 戰撫州唐埠、七里岡、五桂寨、徐汊，屢破敵，復餘乾、東鄉。

translations.literal: He fought at Tangbu, Qiligang, Wuguizhai, and Xucha in Fuzhou, repeatedly defeated the enemy, and recovered Yugan and Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Tangbu, Qiligang, Wuguizhai, and Xucha in Fuzhou, repeatedly defeated the enemy, and recovered Yugan and Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 詔移師湖南，疏言：「江西為廣東咽喉，當江南、湖廣之沖，今三十餘城皆陷賊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the army shifted to Hunan; he memorialized: "Jiangxi is the throat of Guangdong and sits at the crossroads of Jiangnan and Huguang; now more than thirty cities have all fallen to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the army shifted to Hunan; he memorialized: "Jiangxi is the throat of Guangdong and sits at the crossroads of Jiangnan and Huguang; now more than thirty cities have fallen to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 三桂於醴陵造木城，增偽總兵十餘人，兵七萬、倮倮三千，固守萍鄉諸隘。

translations.literal: Sangui at Liling built wooden fortifications, added more than ten false grand generals, had seventy thousand troops and three thousand Luo-Luo, and held fast the passes of Pingxiang and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui at Liling built wooden fortifications, appointed more than ten false grand generals, mustered seventy thousand troops and three thousand Luo-Luo, and held fast the passes around Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 若撤撫州、饒州、都昌諸路防兵盡赴湖南，則諸路復為賊有。

translations.literal: If the garrison troops on the Fuzhou, Raozhou, and Duchang routes are all withdrawn to Hunan, then those routes will again be held by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: If the garrison troops on the Fuzhou, Raozhou, and Duchang routes are all withdrawn to Hunan, those routes will fall to the rebels again.

sentences.zh: 否則，兵勢單弱，不能長驅。

translations.literal: Otherwise the army will be too weak to drive far.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the army will be too weak to advance far.

sentences.zh: 廣東諸路，恐亦多阻。

translations.literal: The routes into Guangdong will also, I fear, meet many obstacles.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the routes into Guangdong will also meet many obstacles.

sentences.zh: 臣欲先平江西，無卻顧憂，然後移師。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes first to pacify Jiangxi without rear anxieties and then shift the army.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes first to pacify Jiangxi without rear anxieties and then shift the army.

sentences.zh: 」疏聞，上令速定江西。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was received, the emperor ordered Jiangxi quickly settled.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was received, the emperor ordered Jiangxi quickly pacified.

sentences.zh: 岳樂督兵攻建昌，精忠將邵連登率數萬人迎戰長興鄉，擊走之，克建昌，並下萬年、安仁。

translations.literal: Yuele supervised troops in attacking Jianchang; Jingzhong's general Shao Liandeng led tens of thousands to meet battle at Changxing township; they were driven off; Jianchang was taken, and Wannian and Anren also fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele supervised the attack on Jianchang; Jingzhong's general Shao Liandeng led tens of thousands to meet battle at Changxing township and was driven off; Jianchang was taken, and Wannian and Anren also fell.

sentences.zh: 師進克廣信，再進克饒州，破敵景德鎮，復克浮梁、樂平。

translations.literal: The army advanced and took Guangxin, advanced again and took Raozhou, defeated the enemy at Jingdezhen, and again took Fuliang and Leping.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced and took Guangxin, advanced again and took Raozhou, defeated the enemy at Jingdezhen, and recovered Fuliang and Leping.

sentences.zh: 分兵徇宜黃、崇仁、樂安，皆下。

translations.literal: Dividing forces he subdued Yihuang, Chongren, and Le'an—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing his forces he subdued Yihuang, Chongren, and Le'an—all fell.

sentences.zh: 並諭降泰和、龍泉、永新、廬陵、永寧及湖廣茶陵諸縣。

translations.literal: He also ordered the surrender of Taihe, Longquan, Yongxin, Luling, Yongning, and the Huguang counties of Chaling and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He also secured the surrender of Taihe, Longquan, Yongxin, Luling, Yongning, and the Huguang counties of Chaling and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 師再進，克靖安、貴溪。

translations.literal: The army advanced again and took Jing'an and Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced again and took Jing'an and Guixi.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「三桂聞臣進取，必固守要害，非綠旗兵無以搜險，非紅衣炮無以攻堅。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "When Sangui hears that your servant is advancing, he is sure to hold fast the strategic points; without Green Banner troops there is no way to search the difficult terrain, and without red-coated cannon there is no way to storm strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "When Sangui hears that your servant is advancing, he is sure to hold the strategic points; without Green Banner troops there is no way to search the difficult terrain, and without red-coated cannon there is no way to storm strongholds.

sentences.zh: 請令提督趙國祚等率所部從臣進討，並敕發新造西洋炮二十。

translations.literal: I beg that the provincial military commander Zhao Guozuo and others be ordered to lead their detachments to follow your servant in the advance, and that twenty newly made Western cannon be issued by edict.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Provincial Military Commander Zhao Guozuo and others be ordered to lead their detachments to follow your servant in the advance, and that twenty newly made Western cannon be issued by edict.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「精忠將張存遣人稱有兵八千屯順昌，俟大軍入閩為應。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Jingzhong's general Zhang Cun sent word that he had eight thousand troops stationed at Shunchang, waiting for the great army to enter Fujian in support.
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized: "Jingzhong's general Zhang Cun sent word that he had eight thousand troops stationed at Shunchang, waiting to support the great army when it entered Fujian.

sentences.zh: 」詔以簡親王喇布專主福建軍事，而趣岳樂赴長沙。

translations.literal: " An edict put Prince Jian Labu in sole charge of Fujian military affairs and urged Yuele on to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict put Prince Jian Labu in sole charge of Fujian military affairs and urged Yuele on to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 十五年，岳樂師克萍鄉，遂薄長沙。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Yuele's army took Pingxiang and then pressed close to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 Yuele's army took Pingxiang and then pressed close to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「敵船集長沙城下，我師無船，難以應敵。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The enemy's boats are gathered below Changsha city; our army has no boats and finds it hard to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The enemy's boats are gathered below Changsha city; our army has no boats and finds it hard to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 長沙附近林木頗盛，請先撥戰艦七十艘，仍令督撫委員伐木造船。

translations.literal: Timber is quite abundant near Changsha; I beg that seventy warships be first allocated, and that the governor-general and governors still commission men to fell timber and build ships.
translations.idiomatic: Timber is quite abundant near Changsha; I beg that seventy warships be allocated first, and that the governor-general and governors commission men to fell timber and build more ships.

sentences.zh: 」如所請。

translations.literal: " As requested.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔曰：「朕聞王復萍鄉，直抵長沙，甚為嘉悅。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict said: "We have heard that the Prince recovered Pingxiang and pressed straight to Changsha, and are greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict said: "We have heard that the Prince recovered Pingxiang and pressed straight to Changsha, and are greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 王其善撫百姓，使困苦得紓；

translations.literal: Let the Prince well comfort the people so that their distress may be relieved;
translations.idiomatic: Let the Prince well comfort the people so that their distress may be relieved;

sentences.zh: 即脅從者皆朕赤子，當加意招徠。

translations.literal: even those who followed under coercion are Our children and should be recruited with special care.
translations.idiomatic: even those who followed under coercion are Our children and should be recruited with special care.

sentences.zh: 」十六年，遣兵破敵瀏陽，斬千餘級，克平江。

translations.literal: " In the sixteenth year he sent troops and defeated the enemy at Liuyang, beheaded more than a thousand, and took Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: " In Kangxi 16 he sent troops, defeated the enemy at Liuyang, beheaded more than a thousand, and took Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 十七年，破敵七家洞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he defeated the enemy at Qijia Cave.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 he defeated the enemy at Qijia Cave.

sentences.zh: 三桂將林興珠等自湘潭來降。

translations.literal: Sangui's generals Lin Xingzhu and others came over from Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's generals Lin Xingzhu and others surrendered from Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 九月，三桂既死，詔趣岳樂進師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, after Sangui had died, an edict urged Yuele to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, after Sangui had died, an edict urged Yuele to advance the army.

sentences.zh: 岳樂請赴岳州調度諸軍。

translations.literal: Yuele asked to go to Yuezhou to coordinate the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele asked to go to Yuezhou to coordinate the various armies.

sentences.zh: 上命大將軍察尼規取岳州，而令岳樂仍攻長沙。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the grand general Cha Ni to plan the taking of Yuezhou, while Yuele was still to attack Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Grand General Cha Ni to plan the taking of Yuezhou, while Yuele was still to attack Changsha.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，岳州降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year Yuezhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 18 Yuezhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 長沙賊亦棄城遁，遂入長沙，遣兵復湘潭。

translations.literal: The rebels at Changsha also abandoned the city and fled; he then entered Changsha and sent troops to recover Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels at Changsha also abandoned the city and fled; he then entered Changsha and sent troops to recover Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 尋會喇布軍克衡州、寶慶，分兵守焉。

translations.literal: Soon he joined Labu's army in taking Hengzhou and Baoding and left troops to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Labu's army in taking Hengzhou and Baoding and left troops to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 復與喇布合軍攻武岡，破敵寶慶岩溪，斬級數百，獲舟四十。

translations.literal: Again he united with Labu's army to attack Wugang, defeated the enemy at Yanxi in Baoding, beheaded several hundred, and captured forty boats.
translations.idiomatic: Again he united with Labu's army to attack Wugang, defeated the enemy at Yanxi in Baoding, beheaded several hundred, and captured forty boats.

sentences.zh: 師次紫陽河，敵於對岸結營，師逕渡，分兵出敵後夾擊之，敵潰走。

translations.literal: The army halted at Ziyang River; the enemy camped on the opposite bank; the army crossed directly, divided troops to strike from behind the enemy in a pincer, and the enemy broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Ziyang River; the enemy camped on the opposite bank; the army crossed directly, divided troops to strike from behind in a pincer, and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 三桂將吳國貴、胡國柱以二萬人守隘，發炮殪國貴，奪隘。

translations.literal: Sangui's generals Wu Guogui and Hu Guozhu with twenty thousand men held the pass; cannon fire killed Guogui and the pass was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's generals Wu Guogui and Hu Guozhu with twenty thousand men held the pass; cannon fire killed Guogui and the pass was taken.

sentences.zh: 貝子彰泰逐敵至木瓜橋，遂克武岡及楓木嶺。

translations.literal: Beizi Zhangtai pursued the enemy to Mugua Bridge and then took Wugang and Fengmuling.
translations.idiomatic: Beizi Zhangtai pursued the enemy to Mugua Bridge and then took Wugang and Fengmuling.

sentences.zh: 詔召岳樂還京師，以敕印付彰泰。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Yuele to the capital and handed the imperial commission and seal to Zhangtai.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Yuele to the capital and handed the imperial commission and seal to Zhangtai.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，下詔褒岳樂功。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year an edict praised Yuele's merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 19 an edict praised Yuele's merit.

sentences.zh: 岳樂至京師，上於盧溝橋南二十里行郊勞禮。

translations.literal: When Yuele reached the capital, the emperor performed the suburban reward ceremony twenty li south of the Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuele reached the capital, the emperor performed the suburban reward ceremony twenty li south of the Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 順治初，故明外戚周奎家有自稱明太子者，使舊宮人及東宮官屬辦視非是。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, in the household of the former Ming imperial affinal kin Zhou Kui there was one who called himself the Ming crown prince; former palace women and Eastern Palace officials were sent to examine him and found he was not.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, in the household of the former Ming imperial affinal kin Zhou Kui there was one who called himself the Ming crown prince; former palace women and Eastern Palace officials were sent to examine him and found he was not genuine.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，京師又有朱慈璊者，自稱三太子，私改元廣德，糾黨舉火為亂，事敗，慈璊走免。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, in the capital there was also Zhu Cihuan, who called himself the third prince, privately changed the era name to Guangde, gathered a faction, and raised fire in revolt; the affair failed and Cihuan escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui rebelled, in the capital there was also Zhu Cihuan, who called himself the third prince, privately changed the era name to Guangde, gathered a faction, and raised fire in revolt; the affair failed and Cihuan escaped.

sentences.zh: 鞫其黨，謂其真姓名為楊起隆。

translations.literal: When his faction was examined, it was said his true name was Yang Qilong.
translations.idiomatic: When his faction was examined, it was said his true name was Yang Qilong.

sentences.zh: 及岳樂駐師楓木嶺，於新化僧寺得朱慈燦，自言為莊烈帝長子，闖難奔南京，福王置諸獄，釋為民，從朽木和尚為僧，往來永州、寶慶間。

translations.literal: When Yuele was stationed at Fengmuling, at a monastery in Xinhua they obtained Zhu Cican, who declared himself the Chongzhen Emperor's eldest son; at the turmoil of the bandit uprising he fled to Nanjing; the Prince of Fu put him in prison, then released him as a commoner; he followed the monk Xiumu and wandered between Yongzhou and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuele was stationed at Fengmuling, at a monastery in Xinhua they obtained Zhu Cican, who declared himself the Chongzhen Emperor's eldest son; at the turmoil of the bandit uprising he fled to Nanjing; the Prince of Fu put him in prison, then released him as a commoner; he followed the monk Xiumu and wandered between Yongzhou and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 以三桂悖逆反覆，將募兵聲討，三桂死，乃止。

translations.literal: Because Sangui was perfidious and turned back and forth, he was about to raise troops to denounce him in a proclamation; when Sangui died he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sangui was perfidious and turned back and forth, he was about to raise troops to denounce him in a proclamation; when Sangui died he stopped.

sentences.zh: 至是，岳樂攜慈燦來京，詔令慈璊黨相見，復不相識，乃斬之。

translations.literal: At this time Yuele brought Cican to the capital; an edict ordered him shown to Cihuan's faction; they again did not recognize one another; he was then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yuele brought Cican to the capital; an edict ordered him shown to Cihuan's faction; they again did not recognize one another; he was then beheaded.

sentences.zh: 二十年，仍掌宗人府事。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he again managed the affairs of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 20 he again managed the affairs of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，偕簡親王雅布往蘇尼特防噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he went with Prince Jian Yabu to the Sunite to guard against Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27 he went with Prince Jian Yabu to the Sunite to guard against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 二十八年二月，薨，予謚。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-eighth year he died; a posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 28 he died; a posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，貝勒諾尼訐岳樂掌宗人府，聽讒，枉坐諾尼不孝罪，追降郡王，削謚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year beile Niohni accused Yuele of managing the Imperial Clan Court, listening to slander, and wrongly convicting Niohni of the crime of unfilial conduct; Yuele was posthumously reduced to prince of the second degree and his posthumous title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 beile Niohni accused Yuele of managing the Imperial Clan Court, listening to slander, and wrongly convicting Niohni of unfilial conduct; Yuele was posthumously reduced to prince of the second degree and his posthumous title was stripped.

sentences.zh: 岳樂子二十，有爵者三：蘊端、瑪爾渾、經希。

translations.literal: Yuele had twenty sons; three held rank: Yunduan, Maerhun, and Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele had twenty sons; three held rank: Yunduan, Maerhun, and Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 蘊端封勤郡王，坐事降貝子；

translations.literal: Yunduan was enfeoffed as Prince Qin of the second degree and, on conviction of an offense, was reduced to beizi;
translations.idiomatic: Yunduan was enfeoffed as Prince Qin of the second degree and, on conviction of an offense, was reduced to beizi;

sentences.zh: 復坐事奪爵。

translations.literal: again on conviction of an offense his title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: again on conviction of an offense his title was stripped.

sentences.zh: 經希封僖郡王。

translations.literal: Jingxi was enfeoffed as Prince Xi of the second degree.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxi was enfeoffed as Prince Xi of the second degree.

sentences.zh: 岳樂得罪，降鎮國公，卒，停襲。

translations.literal: When Yuele fell into disgrace, Jingxi was reduced to Duke Zhenguo; he died and inheritance ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuele fell into disgrace, Jingxi was reduced to Duke Zhenguo; he died and inheritance ceased.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾渾，襲爵。

translations.literal: Maerhun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Maerhun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾渾好學能文章，蘊端亦善詩詞。

translations.literal: Maerhun loved learning and could write essays; Yunduan was also skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Maerhun loved learning and could write essays; Yunduan was also skilled in poetry.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾渾又輯宗室王公詩為宸萼集，一時知名士多從之游。

translations.literal: Maerhun also compiled the poetry of imperial-clan princes and dukes into the Chen'e Collection; many celebrated scholars of the time associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Maerhun also compiled the poetry of imperial-clan princes and dukes into the Chen'e Collection; many celebrated scholars of the time associated with him.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，薨，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he died; his posthumous title was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 48 he died; his posthumous title was Yi.

sentences.zh: 子華玘，襲。

translations.literal: His son Hua Qi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hua Qi inherited.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，薨，謚曰節。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he died; his posthumous title was Jie.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 58 he died; his posthumous title was Jie.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年十二月，詔曰：「曩安郡王岳樂諂附輔政大臣，每觸忤皇考，蒙恩始終寬宥，而其諸子全不知感，傾軋營求，妄冀封爵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Yongzheng an edict said: "Formerly Prince An Yuele fawned on the regent ministers and repeatedly offended Our late father; by grace he was spared to the end, yet his sons altogether failed to feel gratitude, schemed against one another in rivalry, and vainly hoped for enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yongzheng 1 an edict said: "Formerly Prince An Yuele fawned on the regent ministers and repeatedly offended Our late father; by grace he was spared to the end, yet his sons altogether failed to feel gratitude, schemed against one another in rivalry, and vainly hoped for enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾渾、華玘相繼夭折，爵位久懸。

translations.literal: Maerhun and Hua Qi died young in succession, and the title long hung vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Maerhun and Hua Qi died young in succession, and the title long hung vacant.

sentences.zh: 岳樂諸子伍爾占、諸孫色亨圖等，怨望形於辭色。
